clue.text: Family stress

explanation.surface: A household under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a line of descent or breed, and strain is also tension or pressure.

clue.text: Clients' letters bashed out -from this?

indicators.note: letters bashed out are knocked into a new shape, so the word clients is rearranged

explanation.surface: A typist hammers out letters for customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bashed out' rearranges CLIENTS (the possessive apostrophe gives no letter); the whole clue also describes a cut-out sheet through which lettering is painted or printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut template used to reproduce letters, so clients' lettering could be produced from one.

clue.text: Trial from which the public is excluded

definitions.text: Trial from which the public is excluded

parts.words: Trial from which the public is excluded
parts.note: reads like a closed court hearing, but means a private practice run before a performance

explanation.surface: A court case held behind closed doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical run-through is a trial performance that audiences do not attend.

clue.text: Peruvians head east as precaution

indicators.note: the Peruvians come first, heading the compass point that follows them

parts.note: the Incas were the ancient people of Peru
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: South Americans travel eastward to be on the safe side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a safeguard, should something happen.

clue.text: Disapproving expressions, sinister ones

parts.note: grim means forbidding or sinister
an ace is the one in a suit of cards

explanation.surface: Frowns of disapproval that look menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial contortions showing distaste are the classic disapproving looks.

clue.text: Register the sound of a drum

explanation.surface: Take attendance to a drumbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is an official register of names, and a drum roll is a rapid sustained beating.

clue.text: Prodigal female locked up

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
pent means penned or shut in

explanation.surface: A woman has been imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigal life is a wasted one, squandered on extravagance.

clue.text: Saucy thing to cut

explanation.surface: Something cheeky to slice.
explanation.definitionFit: Capers are pickled buds used in sauces, and to cut a caper is to leap playfully.

clue.text: The estate agent's lying

parts.note: suggests a dishonest property seller, but means the agent's word for where a house lies

explanation.surface: A property dealer telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' is not about deceit but position: estate agents describe a house as well placed or sited.
explanation.definitionFit: To place or locate something; agents speak of property being well positioned.

clue.text: Itches to change the rules of conduct

indicators.note: the letters of itches are to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An urge to rewrite the code of behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the moral principles governing behaviour.

clue.text: Top shelf may be the place for titillating entertainment

indicators.note: top shelf may be rearranged into another word, so the phrase signals an anagram

explanation.surface: Racy magazines are kept on the top shelf of a newsagent's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top shelf' is where British shops place adult magazines, so the surface stays on the theme of its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleshpot is a place offering sensual or sleazy amusement.

clue.text: Red hot stuff

parts.note: sounds like slang for something sexy or exciting, but describes a fiery red spice

explanation.surface: Something sensational.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent red chilli powder is literally both red and hot.

clue.text: For which one needs to be in fighting form?

definitions.text: For which one needs to be in fighting form?

parts.words: For which one needs to be in fighting form?
parts.note: suggests physical fitness for a battle, but form here is a school class, so the conflict is between social classes

explanation.surface: Getting fit for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Conflict between social strata, with form read as class.

clue.text: Ancient city seen in pictures in spring

indicators.note: the pictures are placed inside the spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
art means paintings or pictures

explanation.surface: An old town portrayed in paintings of springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek city-state famed for its warriors is a classic ancient city.

clue.text: A really quiet rest can bring calm

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: Silence and relaxation are soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or placate is to restore calm.

clue.text: Pay attention or bend over

explanation.surface: Listen, then lean down.
explanation.definitionFit: List is an old word for listen, and a ship lists when it tilts to one side.

clue.text: Pool of London

parts.note: recalls the stretch of the Thames known as the Pool of London, but means a lake in a London park

explanation.surface: The reach of the Thames below London Bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pool of London is a stretch of the Thames; the answer is instead the lake in Hyde Park, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The winding ornamental lake in Hyde Park is a body of water, a pool, in London.

clue.text: At home, arrange to put in new grass

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the letter for new is put inside the word for arrange

parts.note: to format is to arrange or lay out

explanation.surface: A gardener plans to resow a lawn while staying in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is British slang for a police informer, not the lawn the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for someone who tells the police about criminals.

clue.text: Put up with a girl in New York

parts.note: to brook is to tolerate
Lyn is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Tolerating a girlfriend in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn is one of the five boroughs of New York City.

clue.text: Bob's producer

parts.note: looks like a hairdresser or a man named Bob's TV producer, but a bob is a sequence in change ringing of church bells

explanation.surface: The person behind a show called Bob.
explanation.definitionFit: In change ringing a bob is a set pattern of changes, made by those pulling the church bells.

clue.text: Demonstrate a method of quartering

explanation.surface: Show how to cut something into four.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer or protest noisily, and barracks are quarters for housing soldiers.

clue.text: Hair-style for a transformation?

indicators.note: a transformation alters the arrangement of the words for a

explanation.surface: A hairdo for a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded bushy hairstyle of tightly curled hair.

clue.text: I'd roved around, but went too far

indicators.note: the letters of I'd roved are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller wandered widely but overstepped.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to exaggerate or go to excess.

clue.text: A venue for a match away from home

parts.note: a field is a sports ground where games are played

explanation.surface: A ground for an away fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Far afield means at a distance, away from where one lives.

clue.text: Prospector pops out to see the parson

indicators.note: the letters of pops come out of prospector, and what remains is the answer

explanation.surface: A gold miner nips out to visit the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes the letters P, O, P and S out of PROSPECTOR; they do not sit together in order, and the letters left spell the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a clergyman in charge of a parish.

clue.text: Organ stop

explanation.surface: A pipe-organ control.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is part of the large intestine, and also a punctuation mark, a kind of stop.

clue.text: Refuse CO0 agitating to send the troops in

indicators.note: agitating stirs up the letters of refuse and CO

parts.note: CO, commanding officer, is taken as written

explanation.surface: A commanding officer declines to stir trouble by deploying soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Deploying troops is resorting to military might.

clue.text: Lots of trousers

explanation.surface: Plenty of slacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags means plenty, and Oxford bags are wide-legged trousers.

clue.text: No one doubts what this signal means

definitions.text: No one doubts what this signal means

parts.words: No one doubts what this signal means
parts.note: read literally, everyone finds the meaning obvious, which describes the signal that danger is over

explanation.surface: An unmistakable signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The siren after an air raid tells everyone the danger has passed; read literally, everybody understands it.

clue.text: Consider changing gear on the way

indicators.note: the letters of gear are changed round

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Thinking about shifting gear while driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way' looks like part of the driving picture, but it is the road abbreviation that ends the answer; 'changing' scrambles the gear word to start it.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look upon or think of something in a certain way.

clue.text: Benevolence of a sort shown by the head

parts.note: kind means sort or type
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Charity of some kind from the headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Generosity and goodwill toward others.

clue.text: New deed includes it when revised

indicators.note: the rearranged deed holds the word it inside
a new version of deed has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh legal document incorporates it after redrafting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' scrambles the deed's letters to EDED, and 'includes' holds the clue word it inside them; the surface's legal document is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited text has been corrected and amended.
